name: Noodle soup
standfirst: Cook noodles, get hot broth onto them, put something on top. Every noodle-eating culture arrived at this, and then argued about the broth — whether to keep it clear, boil it cloudy, thicken it with pulses or toasted flour, cut it with coconut, or make it sour. The second argument is quieter: whether the cook finishes the bowl, or you do.
root: Noodles and hot broth in one bowl

dishes.name: Shoyu ramen
dishes.note: The seasoning goes into the empty bowl before the broth does. By the time it reaches you the decision has been made.

dishes.name: Tonkotsu ramen
dishes.note: Same pork bones a clear stock would use, held at a rolling boil instead of a simmer. The noodle is thin because the broth clings to it.

dishes.name: Wonton noodle soup
dishes.note: The dried seafood does the work a long meat stock would do elsewhere — depth without cloudiness.

dishes.name: Lanzhou beef lamian
dishes.note: Judged on the clarity of the broth, which is why the pot is skimmed and never allowed to boil — the beef cooks in it, then comes out to be sliced and laid on at the end.

dishes.name: Hongshao niurou mian
dishes.note: Taiwan's red-braised bowl. Lanzhou's beef cooks in its broth too, but this beef is braised in soy and chilli bean paste first, so the colour goes into the pot and stays.

dishes.name: Kalguksu
dishes.note: The noodles are boiled in the soup rather than beside it, so the flour on them thickens it. The noodle is an ingredient in the broth.

dishes.name: Phở bò
dishes.note: The rare beef is cooked by the broth as it is poured. In the southern bowl everything else happens at your end of the table.

dishes.name: Bún bò Huế
dishes.note: Not a spicy phở. Different bone stock, different noodle, and a shrimp paste that phở would never allow.

dishes.name: Curry laksa
dishes.note: Two noodles in one bowl on purpose — the rice vermicelli carries the broth, the yellow wheat noodle stays springy in it.

dishes.name: Asam laksa
dishes.note: Shares a name with curry laksa and almost nothing else. No coconut at all: the richness is replaced by sourness and raw fruit.

dishes.name: Khao soi
dishes.note: The only bowl here that serves its noodle twice, once soft and once fried, so the texture changes as you eat.

dishes.name: Mohinga
dishes.note: Thickened with toasted rice flour rather than fat or coconut — a third way to make a broth cling.

dishes.name: Soto ayam
dishes.note: The only noodle here made from neither wheat nor rice. Glass noodles are soaked, not boiled, so they never cloud the broth.

dishes.name: Ash reshteh
dishes.note: No stock at all. The pulses are the body of the soup, and the noodles are salted so they season it as they cook.

dishes.name: Chicken noodle soup
dishes.note: The plainest bowl in the family, and the clearest statement of the base: a gently simmered bird, an egg noodle, and nothing hiding. Ashkenazi in origin, and now thoroughly American.

dishes.name: Yaka mein
dishes.note: A Chinese-American noodle soup that stayed in Black New Orleans and kept going. Spaghetti is not a substitution here; it is the noodle.

notes.title: Clear or cloudy is one decision
notes.body: A pot of bones held just under a simmer and skimmed stays transparent — that is Lanzhou beef lamian, and phở. The same bones at a hard rolling boil for eight or twelve hours drive fat and gelatine into suspension until the broth turns opaque and coats the noodle — that is tonkotsu. Nothing else changes. Emulsified broth is not a richer recipe than clear broth; it is a hotter one. Kalguksu clouds a third way, and a cooler one: flour off the noodles, not fat off the bones.

notes.title: Who finishes the bowl
notes.body: A ramen bowl arrives with its seasoning already decided — the tare went into the empty bowl before the broth did, and reaching for the chilli is a comment on the cook. A bowl of phở in Saigon arrives deliberately incomplete, with herbs, lime and chilli on a plate beside it, and assembling it is the last step of the recipe rather than a garnish. Neither bowl is more finished than the other. They put the seasoning decision in different hands.

notes.title: The noodle is chosen for how it behaves in liquid
notes.body: Alkaline wheat noodles resist going soft, which is why they can sit in boiling broth and be eaten slowly. Rice noodles absorb and go slippery, which is why phở is eaten fast. Knife-cut kalguksu noodles are floury on purpose and cloud the broth they cook in. And glass noodles are soaked rather than boiled, so they add nothing to the soup at all — which is exactly what a clear turmeric broth wants.

notes.title: Why nothing here has a parent
notes.body: Every bowl in this family sits at the same depth, because none of them is another one plus a step. Khao soi is not laksa with different noodles and asam laksa is not curry laksa with the coconut taken out — they are separate answers to the same problem, arrived at independently, that happen to share a word. Lineage exists inside each tradition, not between them.
